opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kenneth Burch (employee ID E007) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E007.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, write is the standard maximum; Payroll admin requires the Payroll Specialist role, so write is the appropriate level.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E007 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is above the maximum, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: There is conflicting employee data: HR's note lists E007 as full-time (max write), while the Security DB lists E007 as a contractor with basic security training (max read for contractors without advanced training). Since the two sources conflict on employment type, I apply the more restrictive access consistent with policy: contractor with basic training cannot exceed read, and write is above that maximum. Therefore grant read for Payroll.
